concepts.title: Scalar Product of Two Vectors
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the dot product of two vector quantities produces a scalar value same as the result of multiplying their magnitudes and the angle's cosine between their directions.
concepts.formula: dot_product = ax * bx + ay * by + az * bz
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the scalar product evaluates the projection of one vector along the direction of another.

solution_steps.action: multiply corresponding component values and sum them

concepts.title: Work-Energy Theorem for Constant Force
concepts.definition: The net work performed on a particle by the vector sum of all acting forces is equal to the resulting change in the particle's kinetic energy.
concepts.key_idea: Net work done on a body directly increases or decreases its kinetic energy.
question_patterns: calculate work done using change in kinetic energy
find the work done by resistive force on a falling drop
determine work done on a raindrop using initial and final speeds
what is the net work done on a moving particle

solution_steps.action: calculate initial kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Initial kinetic energy depends on mass and initial speed.

solution_steps.action: calculate final kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Final kinetic energy depends on mass and final speed.

solution_steps.action: compute net work done
solution_steps.explain: Net work equals final kinetic energy minus initial kinetic energy.

concepts.title: Work Done by a Constant Force
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, work done by a constant force means the result of multiplying the magnitude of both both both both both both both both both both both both both displacement and the constituent of force in the direction of that displacement.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Work is a scalar amount that varies with force, displacement, and the angle between them.
question_patterns: find the work done by a constant force
calculate the work when force is applied at an angle to displacement
what is the work done on a displaced object
compute the work done against friction

solution_steps.action: multiply force, displacement, and cosine of angle
solution_steps.explain: Work equals magnitude of force times magnitude of displacement times cosine of the angle between them.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy
concepts.definition: In brief, Kinetic energy represents the capacity of an object to do work purely by virtue of its state of motion.
concepts.key_idea: Kinetic energy is a positive scalar quantity proportional to mass and the square of velocity.
question_patterns: find the kinetic energy of a moving body
calculate the kinetic energy given mass and speed
what is the emergent speed of a bullet losing part of its kinetic energy
compute the final kinetic energy after speed reduction

solution_steps.action: calculate kinetic energy from mass and speed
solution_steps.explain: Kinetic energy is half mass times speed squared.

concepts.title: Work Done by a Variable Force
concepts.definition: The total work performed by a position-varying force equals the area under the force-versus-position curve across the displacement interval.
concepts.key_idea: Variable work is calculated by summing linear or rectangular sub-areas under a force-position graph.
question_patterns: calculate work done by a variable force
find work done from a force versus displacement graph
determine work done by a linearly reducing force
compute total work done over multiple path segments

solution_steps.action: calculate work in constant force interval
solution_steps.explain: Area of rectangle gives work in first segment.

solution_steps.action: calculate work in linearly changing force interval
solution_steps.explain: Area of trapezium gives work in second segment.

solution_steps.action: sum work contributions
solution_steps.explain: Total work is the sum of work over all segments.

concepts.title: Work-Energy Theorem for Variable Force
concepts.definition: The definite integral of a variable force over a spatial interval equals the net change in kinetic energy between the boundary positions.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Integrating force with respect to displacement yields the net kinetic energy change.
question_patterns: calculate final kinetic energy for a spatially variable retarding force
find final speed after passing through a variable force region

compute kinetic energy change under position dependent force

solution_steps.action: calculate initial kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Determine starting kinetic energy from initial speed.

solution_steps.action: add integrated work done to initial kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Final kinetic energy equals initial kinetic energy plus integral of force over displacement.

solution_steps.action: calculate final speed from final kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Speed is square root of twice kinetic energy divided by mass.

concepts.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
concepts.definition: Gravitational potential energy is energy stored within a system due to the vertical elevation of an object against Earth's gravitational pull.
concepts.key_idea: Potential energy reflects stored capacity for mechanical work based on vertical position.
question_patterns: calculate gravitational potential energy
find potential energy at height h
what is the stored energy of an elevated mass
compute potential energy change when height increases

solution_steps.action: compute potential energy from mass, acceleration of gravity, and height
solution_steps.explain: Multiply mass, acceleration due to gravity, and height.

concepts.title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the total mechanical energy of an isolated system remains constant over time provided all internal working forces are conservative.
concepts.formula: total_energy = (1/2) * mass * speed**2 + mass * g * height
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Kinetic and potential energies convert into one another while their total sum stays fixed.
question_patterns: find speed at bottom of trajectory using energy conservation

solution_steps.action: determine initial total mechanical energy
solution_steps.explain: Total energy at top is purely gravitational potential energy.

solution_steps.action: calculate final speed assuming total conversion to kinetic energy
solution_steps.explain: Equate total energy to kinetic energy at ground level.

concepts.title: Potential Energy of a Spring
concepts.definition: The work required to stretch or compress an ideal spring by a distance x gets stored as elastic potential energy proportional to the square of deformation.
concepts.key_idea: Hooke's law spring force stores elastic energy quadratically with compression or extension.
question_patterns: find maximum compression of a spring

solution_steps.action: solve for maximum spring compression assuming full energy conversion
solution_steps.explain: Equate initial kinetic energy to spring potential energy at maximum compression.

concepts.title: Power
concepts.definition: Power measures the temporal rate of doing work or transferring energy, expressed as scalar product of force and velocity.
concepts.key_idea: Power quantifies how rapidly mechanical work is supplied by a source.
question_patterns: calculate minimum power required by an elevator motor
find power delivered given force and speed
convert power from watts to horsepower
compute electric power consumed in lifting a load

solution_steps.action: calculate total opposing downward force
solution_steps.explain: Sum of gravitational weight and opposing resistive friction force.

solution_steps.action: compute power delivered in watts
solution_steps.explain: Power equals total opposing force multiplied by constant speed.

solution_steps.action: convert power to horsepower
solution_steps.explain: Divide power in watts by 746 to obtain horsepower.

concepts.title: One-Dimensional Elastic Collision
concepts.definition: A head-on impact between two bodies in which total linear momentum and total kinetic energy are both conserved.
concepts.key_idea: Elastic collisions preserve both linear both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both momentum and kinetic energy post-impact.

concepts.title: Two-Dimensional Collisions
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, a planar impact where linear momentum vectors are conserved independently along perpendicular axes.
concepts.key_idea: Glancing elastic collisions between equal masses with one at rest result in perpendicular trajectories.
